transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
My eating has gotten all mixed up. Some days I forget lunch entirely, and other days I’m standing at the counter eating crackers and sweets, even though nothing really tastes right.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or finding little interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
Most mornings, yes. I wake up with this heavy, low feeling, like the color has gone out of the day before I even get dressed.
How long have you been experiencing this low mood and the changes in your eating—days, weeks, or longer?
It’s been going on for about a year and two months now—the low, colorless feeling and the eating changes.
Over this past year and two months, has there been any stretch of two months or more where you felt completely back to your normal mood, without the low, colorless feeling?
No, I can’t think of a two-month stretch where I felt back to normal. It’s been that low, colorless feeling for about a year and two months.

During this past year, has there been a period of at least two weeks where your mood or energy became noticeably worse than your usual baseline—for example, with major sleep changes, loss of energy, trouble concentrating, or thoughts of worthlessness or death?
Yes. There have been stretches where it feels worse—most mornings I wake up with this heavy, low feeling, like all the color has gone out of the day before I even get dressed.
When you find yourself eating crackers and sweets like that, do you feel like you can't control or stop the eating once you start?
Some days I do just keep standing there eating crackers and sweets, even though nothing really tastes right. Other days I forget lunch altogether. My eating just feels all turned around.
During those worse stretches, have you had feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt about yourself?
I’m not sure I’d call it guilt or worthlessness exactly. I mostly just feel low and sort of empty.
During those worse stretches, have you noticed significant changes in your sleep—like sleeping much more or much less than usual?
I haven’t really noticed a big change in my sleep, no.
When you have those worse stretches of low mood, how long do they typically last—days, or do they go on for two weeks or more at a time?
It’s been going on a long time, not just days. I’d say about a year and two months now.
During those worse stretches, have you noticed a significant drop in your energy level or new difficulty concentrating on tasks?
Yes, concentrating has been harder. I’ll sit there looking at something simple, like whether to call the pharmacy or open the mail first, and my mind gets so foggy I end up doing neither.
After those times when you eat the crackers and sweets like that, do you feel upset, ashamed, or distressed about having eaten that way?

I do feel upset about it. It’s like my eating is all turned around—some days I forget lunch, and then other days I’m standing there eating crackers and sweets, even though nothing really tastes right.
When you're eating the crackers and sweets, do you end up eating a much larger amount than most people would in that same short period of time?

I don’t know if it’s much more than other people, exactly. I just find myself standing there eating crackers and sweets, and it doesn’t even taste right. Other days I forget lunch completely, so my eating has gotten very mixed up.
During these worse stretches, have you had any thoughts about death or that you'd be better off not being alive?
I don’t have a plan to hurt myself. But sometimes I think that if I didn’t wake up one morning, it might be a relief to everyone.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy nearly every day during this time?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed being unusually tired every day.
Thinking about your most recent worse stretch, has it lasted continuously for at least two weeks in a row, or does it come and go day to day?
I'm not really sure. I haven't kept track of it closely enough to say whether it was two weeks straight.
During this time, have you noticed a significant change in your weight—either losing or gaining a noticeable amount—without trying to?
I’m not sure about my weight, but my eating has gotten all mixed up. Some days I forget lunch, and other days I just stand there eating crackers and sweets, even though nothing really tastes right.
During those worse stretches of low mood, have others noticed you moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or alternatively, have you felt unusually restless or fidgety?

Yes. Lately my body feels slowed down—like it takes me twice as long just to cross the room or button my sweater. But then sometimes I’ll pace around the house holding the same papers, not really doing anything with them.
Over just the last two weeks, would you say these symptoms—the low mood, trouble concentrating, slowed movements, and eating changes—have been present nearly every single day without a break?
It’s been more than just the last two weeks. This low, colorless feeling has been with me for about a year and two months.
During this time, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy?
Yes. I used to look forward to watercolor class, quilting circle, and book club. Now I’ll have my bag by the door and just... can’t make myself care enough to go.

Before this past year and two months began, had you ever gone through a separate period—lasting at least two weeks—of similarly low, colorless mood at some earlier point in your life, with a return to your normal self in between?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of a separate time like that where I got back to feeling like myself in between.
